description: DRV2605L I2C haptic motor driver breakout

electrical.note: The driver itself is small; the MOTOR is the transient. A typical coin ERM motor draws roughly 100-156 mA at start, which is well above the 100 mA threshold that demands local bulk capacitance.

i2c.address_select: Fixed. Two DRV2605Ls cannot share a bus without an I2C multiplexer.

liveness_check.how: A haptic that stops buzzing produces no error. Read back the device ID register on boot, and make at least one startup pulse observable to the user.

traps: The address is FIXED at 0x5A. Check it against everything else on the bus before committing.
The motor is an inductive load. It needs a flyback path and local bulk capacitance, sited at the driver, not at the battery connector.
A vibration motor is a mechanical noise source. It will be heard by any unsealed microphone in the same enclosure.
notes: Set the LRA/ERM mode and run the auto-calibration for the specific motor. A driver configured for the wrong motor type works badly rather than failing, which is the worst kind of wrong.
